title: Quarterly Constellation Plan: Hosted API Release Windows & Model Cohort Phasing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a repeatable quarterly plan for coordinating Hosted API release windows with model-catalog cohort phasing. Goal is to deliver a predictable cadence of model variants and endpoint changes that balances reliability (SLOs), cost (batching/quantization hedges), and product velocity.

Scope: planning artifacts, rollout windows, canary criteria, evaluation gate definitions, capacity reserve hedges, and stakeholder playbooks covering Hosted API, Dedicated capacity signals, and Console observability. This ticket captures the top-level roadmap, decision trade-offs, and the phased schedule for Q2 execution.

Objectives / OKRs: 
- OKR-1 (Reliability): Maintain 99.9% p99 latency SLO for primary hosted routes during model rotations.
- OKR-2 (Cost): Reduce per-token cost for inference-heavy endpoints by 12% via recommended quantization and batching profiles.
- OKR-3 (Quality): Zero-production regressions on core customer prompt sets during scheduled rotations (measured by eval set pass rate >= 95%).

Key decisions to land: 
- Adopt cohort phasing (A/B cohort percentages) rather than fleet-wide immediate swaps for major model upgrades.
- Default canary window of 48h for low-risk minor variants, 72h + load simulation for major upstream changes.
- Reserve a 15% capacity hedge in Dedicated pools for peak-week releases.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Faster fleet-wide swaps reduce ops burden but increase risk of regressing customer experience. Cohort phasing costs ops time to monitor but isolates regressions.
- Stronger batching/quantization reduces cost but may increase tail latency; decide per-route SLOs.

Gating criteria for each cohort rollout: 
- CI/evals green on canonical prompt sets and targeted safety checks.
- Synthetic load test at 110% of expected 95th percentile QPS for the route.
- No escalations from CS/Customer signals in last 7 days for the same endpoint.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook with clear release windows and cohort phasing steps is published to Confluence. 2) Canary checklist produced and reviewed by Eng + CS. 3) Eval harness runs successfully against three representative endpoints with pass rate >=95%. 4) Capacity reserve plan documented and communicated to Dedicated operations. 5) Stakeholder sign-off (Eng, PM, CS, Security).
risks:
- Unexpected model regressions during cohort expansions could impact high-volume customers.
- Capacity overcommit if reserve hedges not provisioned in time for release weeks.
- Gating evals may miss latent prompt regressions for niche cohorts.
- Cross-team synchronization failures (Console vs Serving vs Orchestration) could delay rollouts.
rollout_schedule: Phase 0: Planning & artifacts (Mar 10 - Mar 21): finalize PRD, canary checklist, eval prompts
Phase 1: Dry-run + synthetic load (Mar 22 - Apr 2): run synthetic traffic + validation
Phase 2: Canary cohorts (Apr 5 - Apr 11): 5% -> 20% expansion on low-risk endpoints
Phase 3: Staggered fleet expansion (Apr 12 - Apr 30): route-by-route rollout with monitoring gates
Phase 4: Post-rollout retrospective (May 5 - May 12): traffic & cost analysis, runbook updates
